full_judgment: 10. Lastly, it has been contended by the learned Advocate for the appellants that admittedly 21 witnesses were cited in the charge-sheet and out of them only 10 have been produced in court but the most material witnesses in this case are the driver Mati Mia and the other helpers numbering about 5 of the said bus of occurrence who were also suspected to be involved in the alleged dacoity, but they have neither been accused nor witnesses in this case and produced in the court. It has been contended by the learned Advocate for the appellants that the trial Court committed illegality in not drawing an adverse presumption against the genuineness of the case for non-production of the above persons in court. The learned Advocate for the State has submitted that the prosecution is not bound to produce all the witnesses cited in the charge sheet and that even on the basis of the evidence of a single witness, conviction can be maintained. The contention is not disputed, but in the facts and circumstances of the present case when not a single witness of such quality is available particularly to identify the dacoits the necessity of producing the other material witnesses named in charge-sheet cannot be under estimated and hence non-production of such witnesses naturally gives rise to an adverse presumption against the prosecution case. Further it appears that all the appellants have been convicted under sections 395/397 of the Penal Code and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 10 years. Section 397 of the Penal Code has limited the minimum sentence to 7 years, if the case is proved against the accused under that section. In the entire case, we find that there is no allegation of carrying any deadly weapon by the accused appellants as required under section 397 of the Penal Code, and also there is no reliable and sufficient evidence to prove any such allegation of carrying any deadly weapon or weapons by the appellants, not to speak of using the same against any of the victims. Therefore, in any view of the matter, the conviction of the appellants under section 397 is wholly bad and illegal and cannot stand in law. However, having considered all aspects of the matter, the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record including laws and decisions referred to above, we are of the view that in fact this is a case of no evidence against the appellants as contended on their behalf and the prosecution has hopelessly failed to prove the charges leveled against them beyond all reasonable doubt. In view of the above, we are therefore inclined to give appellants benefit of doubt considering the evidence on record, the co-called confessions and the facts and circumstances of the case.
